thread:
Anya K: Quick heads-up 00: we hit two tenant OOMs last night where background demote/evict churned hot pages during a rolling inference wave. I want to propose a tenant-aware eviction gating surface so compaction/evictors don't treat all tenants equally.

Devon S: Oof. Do you have a minimal repro or traces? I saw a weird DMA spike on shard-7 around 02:17.

Anya K: Putting the traces in the PR, but summary: tenant A was mid-batch, tenant B's aggressive background demote reclaimed pages and kicked the hotset, forcing recompute and high tail.

Ravi M: Tenant-aware gating sounds right. What shape are you thinking for the API?

Anya K: Minimal: allocator exposes shrink_hint(tenant_id, pages_worth, urgency_hint) which returns an op handle. The caller (coordinator / background jobs) can query progress and safe_abort. The key is the allocator can decline or slow work for tenants currently above a hotset threshold.

Kira T: I'd rather call it soft_demote(tenant, budget_bytes, priority). semantics: best-effort; if tenant is hot, allocator returns NEEDS_DELAY or a suggested backoff window.

Devon S: We should be careful about semantics: if allocator just says "no" always then background maintenance starves. Need a debt model: if we defer N times, debt increases and eventually we force a reclaim in a quiet window.

Anya K: Agreed. Sketch of primitives:

// pseudo-interface
op = Allocator::soft_demote_async(tenant_id, budget_bytes, urgency)
status = Allocator::soft_demote_query(op) // "progress_pct", "safe_abort"
Allocator::soft_demote_cancel(op) // only if safe_abort==true
Allocator::mark_tenant_sensitive(tenant_id, until_ts) // SRE/route-level override

Ravi M: Where do we compute "sensitive"? Routing plane? I don't think allocator should pull routing data. Keep allocator local and let coordinator feed hints.

Kira T: Exactly. Coordinator looks at per-tenant p99/p999, kv-hit ratio, and ingress queue depth and surfaces a boolean hint to allocator. Allocator returns one of {ACCEPT, SUGGEST_BACKOFF(ms), REJECT}.

Devon S: A few tradeoffs: (1) estimator quality: hotset detection mustn't be too noisy; (2) eviction cost model: evicting a page might mean recompute cost >> reclaim benefit. We need a reuse-score per page to estimate expected recompute penalty.

Anya K: For reuse-score we can piggyback on kvcache hits + last_access_ts buckets. Not perfect but cheap. Also maintain per-tenant "reclaimability" score aggregated from free-span counts and fragmentation ratio.

Ravi M: Another idea: introduce a preflight mode where allocator simulates reclaim and returns a predicted latency cost (cheap model) before committing. Coordinator uses that to weigh against debt.

Kira T: That could work if prediction is cheap. Maybe a sampling-based estimator: examine N candidate pages and extrapolate. Keep it bounded to avoid lock contention.

Devon S: Operational hooks: allow SRE to tag tenants as 'preserve-hotset' for a rollout, or 'force-reclaim' for cleanup windows. Expose metrics: allocator.soft_demote.requests, rejections, deferred_debt, predicted_cost_estimates.

Anya K: Telemetry plan: emit events with reason tag: manual, debt_flush, low_cpu_window, scheduled_maintenance. Add a gauge per-tenant reclaim_debt that increments when we skip work and decays slowly.

Ravi M: How about tradeoffs re: prefetch vs eviction? If we evict and then immediately prefetch for the same tenant, we waste DMA. Coordinator should prefer moving cold tenants first or schedule eviction during prefetch-windows.

Kira T: We could bias eviction ordering by predicted reuse_score / dma_cost. Heuristic: prefer pages with low reuse_score AND high fragmentation contribution.

Devon S: Experiments we need:
- baseline (current global background evict) with synthetic mixed-tenant bursts
- soft_demote with SUGGEST_BACKOFF and debt accumulation
- soft_demote + preflight cost-estimate enabled
Metrics: tenant tail p99/p999, bytes reclaimed, DMA traffic, fraction of forced long reclaims, reclaim CPU cost.

Anya K: Implementation plan: I'll add soft_demote_async stub in allocator branch that returns REJECT for now. Ravi can wire coordinator feedback loop to call with ingress p99 and kv-hit ratios. Kira, can you help design default thresholds for debt and hotset?

Ravi M: Yep, will prototype coordinator. Quick note: keep abort semantics well-defined: if safe_abort false, cancel fails and caller must schedule a retry later.

Kira T: Agree. Also keep backward-compat: if allocator doesn't implement soft_demote, coordinator falls back to global maintenance schedule.

infra-bot: Metric stream 'allocator.soft_demote.events' will be available in staging at 05:30 UTC.

Devon S: One more thought: users with dedicated capacity should bypass soft_demote gating (customer SLA). Add a serving_profile flag to override.

Anya K: Good call. We'll expose priority in the reason-tag and allocator will honor dedicated_tenant override.

Ravi M: I'll sketch a small perf harness to replay tenant mixes and measure regressions.

Kira T: I'll draft a short design note for /docs/runtime/allocators describing the API, signals and telemetry. Keep it 1-pager.

Anya K: Thanks all. Adding folks to the PR for early feedback. Ping me if you want to join perf runs. :rocket:
